notes: Investigated for genuine Christmas/Halloween/Diwali/Easter/Valentine's/Thanksgiving/New Year or any other holiday category. Tier 1 (HTTP): robots.txt checked first (generic 'User-agent: *' rules only, no Claude-specific disallow, so no policy_opt_out). Fetched both sitemaps (sitemap_en_ca.xml, sitemap_fr_ca.xml, 3488 total <loc> URLs) and regex-scanned every URL for christmas/xmas/noel/halloween/diwali/easter/valentine/thanksgiving/holiday/seasonal/festive/hanukkah/santa/reindeer/pumpkin/witch/diya/rakhi/snowman/sapin/paques/citrouille/mardi-gras/carnival/eid/ramadan/nowruz/ornament/wreath/garland/advent/new-year — only non-PLP inspiration/blog posts matched ('festive-bedroom-bliss', 'holiday-dining-delight', 'inspiration/category/seasonal', 'inspiration/tag/holidays', 'new-year-new-trends/styles'), which are editorial blog articles, not category PLPs, so excluded per rule. Also listed every /decor/* URL in the sitemap (wall-decor, lighting, home-accents and their sub-nodes only) and every top-level lookbook/style-guide slug (e.g. 'harvest-dinner', 'evergreen-dining', 'a-golden-touch') — none are named after a specific holiday and a direct curl of harvest-dinner returned only the bare CSR app shell with no holiday text, confirming these are generic style/mood lookbook pages, not holiday PLPs. Homepage and a sample category page (catalog/category/view/id/248) were fetched directly and returned only the Structube SPA shell ('Oops! JavaScript is disabled' fallback), confirming the site is a client-rendered PWA/SPA, so Tier 1 alone cannot see the real DOM. Escalated to Tier 2 (Playwright/Chromium, installed via npx for this task) per the access-tier rule: rendered the homepage with networkidle and extracted every anchor in the fully rendered DOM, including the full mega-menu for FURNITURE, DECOR, MATTRESSES, NEW, OPEN BOX, SALE, SMALL BUDGET, TOP VALUE, PREMIUM and INSPIRATION. Full taxonomy captured: Furniture > Living Room/Dining Room/Bedroom/Office/Entryway/Storage & Organization/Outdoor (with their sub-categories); Decor > Wall Decor/Lighting/Home Accents (with sub-categories); Mattresses > 5 named mattress collections (LOFT, ICY, ROYAL, HOTEL, ZENITH — brand/product-line names, not holidays); New > Furniture; Open Box; Sale; Small Budget; Top Value; Premium; Inspiration (blog). No node anywhere in this rendered nav is named after or tied to a specific holiday/festival/seasonal event. French sitemap (sitemap_fr_ca.xml) was scanned with the same French-language holiday terms (noel, paques, saint-valentin, action-de-grace, nouvel-an, etc.) with zero matches, confirming the French-Canadian site mirrors the same non-seasonal taxonomy. No Christmas/Halloween/Diwali/Easter/Valentine's/Thanksgiving/New Year (or any other festival) category, sub-category, or landing PLP exists anywhere on structube.com. Concluding NO_SEASONAL with high confidence given the exhaustive sitemap keyword scan plus a full rendered mega-menu extraction, not merely an internal search test.
